question.problem: The hospital emergency room receives an average of $7$ patients per hour. What is the probability that it receives fewer than $4$ patients in the next hour? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that patients arrive independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of patients in the hospital emergency room. Since the average rate is $7$ patients per hour, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of patients can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =7,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(7).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{7}^{x}{e}^{-7}}{x!}
$$

Therefore, the probability of having fewer than $4$ patients in the next hour is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<4) & =P(X\in {0,1,2,3}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2)+f(3) \\  & =\frac{{7}^{0}{e}^{-7}}{0!}+\frac{{7}^{1}{e}^{-7}}{1!}+\frac{{7}^{2}{e}^{-7}}{2!}+\frac{{7}^{3}{e}^{-7}}{3!} \\  & ≈0.082\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
